current_example.problem: The equation $\log_{2}\left( \dfrac{1}{8} \right) = -3$ is equivalent to $b^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{8}.$ What is the value of $b?$
current_example.worked_solution:
The logarithm of $a$ with base $b$ is defined as follows:

$\log_{b}{a} = x$ is equivalent to $a = b^x$

If we compare $\log_{2}\left( \dfrac{1}{8} \right) = -3$ with $\log_{b}{a} = x,$ we get $a = \dfrac{1}{8},$ $b = 2,$ and $x = -3.$

Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to $2^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{8}.$ Consequently, $b = 2.$
